summary:
# NOTES: *Dorothy at Skyrie* by Evelyn Raymond (Gutenberg #41117, 1907, Platt & Peck). Single book. 20 chapters.

## Cast
- **Dorothy Chester** ("Dorothy C.", "Dolly", "Dolly darling"): heroine, adopted, b. April 2. Brown eyes, curly dark hair. Formerly kidnapped to Miranda Stott's truck-farm in Maryland; rescued with help of **Jim Barlow**. Reads Dickens (Barnaby Rudge).
- **John Chester** ("Johnnie", "Dad", "father John"): adoptive father, ex-postman, lame, uses crutches ("wooden feet"). Witty, cheerful.
- **Martha Chester** ("mother Martha", "Martha"): adoptive mother, practical, fretful, proud, anxious about money and debt. Farmer's daughter by memory.
- **Jim Barlow**: ~teen, tall, sunburned, blunt, uneducated truck-farm speech ("Pshaw!", "Shucks!", "Mis'"). Works for Mrs. Calvert at Deerhurst (lodge). Hates shoes. Loves dogs. Wants education; "study" nightly; wants to be President / write Shakespeare-like book. Given books by Mrs. Calvert (a Bible-like "Shakespeare"). Jealous of Herbert.
- **Mrs. Elisabeth Cecil Somerset-Calvert** ("Mrs. Betty Calvert", "Mrs. Cecil", "Betty"): ~80 years old, of Maryland, owns Deerhurst; Great Danes **Peter** and **Ponce**; coachman **Ephraim** (colored; wife/"Miss Betty"); horses **bays**. Wants to adopt Dorothy. Calls Seth "Cousin Seth".
- **Seth Winters**: "Learned Blacksmith", justice of the peace, up-mountain smithy near Great Balm of Gilead tree; weekly paper; benign, Socialist-minded, gave money away. Organizes the Bee. Cousin/old friend of Mrs. Calvert (fathers' estates side by side in old Maryland).
- **Peter Piper**: half-wit, tall, gaunt, white face, white hair, parade hat with red cock feathers, glittering buckle, leather/scarlet jacket; lives in Waterman's mine ("Folly"), gardened Skyrie secretly as "ghost"; saves Dorothy from fall, and Herbert's and Jim's situation.
- **Brindle**: old cow, a pest.
- **Archibald Montaigne** ("Mr. Montaigne"): rich, snob, new money, Deerhurst neighbor, builds mansion "the Towers" on Heights. Eyeglasses. Coachman **James**.
- **Mrs. Montaigne**: timid, kind.
- **Helena Montaigne**: 14, blonde, blue eyes, frail, "delicate" (bronchial), haughty, faints; governess Miss Milliken.
- **Herbert Montaigne**: ~16, handsome, rugged, friendly, horse **Bucephalus** (black). Rakes hay, rescues Mrs. Montaigne, loves Dorothy, plans camp-picnic, gives stray kitten **Kit** to Dorothy.
- **Alfaretta Babcock** ("Alfy", "Sis"), **Baretta** ("Retty"), **Claretta** ("Clary"), **Diaretta** (baby); mother **Mrs. Babcock** (licks children Saturday nights), father **Pa Babcock** (self-styled "Nanarchist", red hair, huge whiskers, lazy, big words). Cat Hollow home. Brothers Matthew, Mark, Luke, John (hired out); three dead.
- **Oliver Sands** ("Friend Oliver", "Thee"): Quaker miller, Heartsease farm, mortgage-holder; "slick trader"; sells Hannah cow for $50 with calf **Daisy-Jewel** free (Jewel → Daisy); lends $300 "payable on demand".
- **Miranda Stott**: truck-farmer, Maryland.
- **Mrs. Smith** (wife of John Smith, neighbor; "Mis' Smith"): mistress of ceremonies at Bee. Smith boys.
- **Bill Barry**: village auctioneer and horse trader; sells Bill's horses; sells widow's piebald pony.
- **Mr. Spence**: postmaster Lower Riverside. Also Mrs. Turnbull, Sarah Spencer (cherry pie).
- **Kidder & Kidder**: Baltimore law firm of Mrs. Calvert; hold Dorothy's fund.
- **Eliza Jane ("'Liza Jane")**: store in other village.
- **Simon Waterman**: former owner of Skyrie, crazy, dug "gold mine" ("Si Waterman's Folly") in south meadow; dog-churn "Hendrick Hudson".
- **Judge Satterlee / Mis' Satterlee**: wealthy neighbor.
- **Mrs. Cecil's Great Danes**: Peter and Ponce.
- **Hannah**: écru-colored cow. **Portia**: piebald calico pony, bought by Dorothy for $35 (seven banknotes). **Lady Rosalind**: Dorothy's cat.
- **Mr. Chester's wheel-chair**: gift from old post-office comrades; rented.

## Places
Skyrie cottage (stone, Highlands of Hudson, Hudson River, mountain; upper and lower Riverside villages; Newburgh; Cat Hollow; Heartsease; the Towers; Deerhurst; Heights; Landing; south meadow; home-piece; cornfield; Headquarters (Washington) in Newburgh). 77 Brown Street, Baltimore (old home). Lexington Market.

## Chapter Events
**I. Early Visitors**: Dorothy picks wild strawberries; Babcock girls appear ("Alfaretta, Baretta, Claretta, Diaretta"). Alfy claims to know Dorothy's history (foundling, kidnapping, Barlow boy, Mrs. Calvert). Berry-picking. Dorothy says she's never been struck. Alfy: Saturday lickings. Pail of berries taken to Mrs. Chester. Alfy: "kidnapped again?"

**II. An Unfortunate Affair**: Jim arrives with basket and letter from Mrs. Calvert; Dorothy teases him about the "haunted" house and garden. Mrs. Calvert's letter for Mr. Chester. Alfy greets Jim ("hero"). Jim flees; dogs Peter and Ponce escape down road; Lower Riverside, mad-dog alarm. Ephraim refastens dogs. Jim knocks down **Archibald Montaigne** in post office; punches him; postmaster Spence. Montaigne says he'll find justice (Seth Winters). Seth takes Jim along.

**III. On the Road to South Meadow**: Breakfast; Alfy's chatter about family. Mrs. Chester hides letter. Alfy: letter read-ingest. Alfy begs to wheel Mr. Chester in wheel-chair; chair overturns into ditch (Alfy steering). Ghost story: Alfy says ghost "he" lives in room where Mr. Chester sleeps and in the gold mine.

**IV. The Learned Blacksmith**: Seth and Jim in ravine; Seth reveals knowledge of Jim's story; caterpillar anecdote. Seth refuses job. Jim at Deerhurst confesses to Mrs. Calvert; dogs return home alone. Mrs. Calvert jealous: "they went to that farm boy first!"

**V. An Accident and an Apparition**: Chair overturns; Mr. Chester bruised, dash of water (Alfy). Mrs. Chester's worry. Mrs. Chester wants money for cow/horse/pig; Mr. Chester's "Want Ad": "Immediate. Pig. Cow. Horse. Skyrie." Alfy smashes dog-churn with ax. Peter Piper appears leading Brindle.

**VI. More Peculiar Visitors**: Peter with Brindle (cow). Alfy explains Brindle, Seth, Pa Babcock. Babcocks depart. Dorothy sings "Annie Laurie". Constable of Lower Riverside serves Dorothy a subpoena for a hearing at Seth's shop, 10 a.m. next day.

**VII. At the Office of a Justice**: Mrs. Smith gossips. Trial at Seth's: Dorothy testifies. Mrs. Calvert appears; Montaigne withdraws complaint, apologizes; Mrs. Cecil introduces Helena (blonde, 14) and Mrs. Montaigne; Herbert (rides Bucephalus, handsome, frank) arrives. Mrs. Calvert pats horse. Mrs. Calvert gives Montaigne a ride; Chester rides in Montaigne carriage. Jim vanishes.

**VIII. A Walk and Its Ending**: Mrs. Chester and Mrs. Cecil walk home happily; currant jelly. Herbert with Dorothy: invites to planked shad at camp on Point, wants her to fish; Dorothy refuses ("I'd feel like a murderer"); Herbert leaves annoyed. Mrs. Cecil says Dorothy likes Herbert; Dorothy praises Jim. Jim working on celery. Turn in road reveals a crowd of horses, cows, pigs.

**IX. A Live Stock Sale**: Montaigne carriage spooked by pigs and cows (from advertisement). Helena faints; Dorothy brings water in cracked pitcher; Mrs. Cecil invites Montaigne to Deerhurst (Helena). Traders shout. Mrs. Chester organizes the purchase: one pig (scrubbed, pinkish-white), one cow, one horse. Oliver Sands sells Hannah (écru cow) for $50 and gives her calf free to Dorothy.

**X. At Milking-Time**: Oliver Sands profile (mortgages; "slick trader"). Bill Barry's jibes. Dorothy names calf Jewel. Jim comes; Mrs. Calvert sends letter. Mrs. Chester offers Jim job; he refuses. Jim's jealousy; Dorothy hugs and kisses him, he rebuffs. Jim says "I'll come work for you", Pa Babcock interrupts: "I've come to hire out."

**XI. Helpers**: Pa Babcock (hired, $2.50/day, every other day, self-board). Oliver Sands offers loan; Mrs. Chester takes it, against husband's wishes. Storm. Mrs. Chester's disagreement with husband; "shadow" between them.

**XII. Seth Winters and His Friends**: Seth organizes "Bee" (Mrs. Calvert approves). Mrs. Chester and Pa Babcock on asparagus; Hannah escapes walls; Dorothy chases her. Dorothy's hands blistered. Bee arrives: "We are nothing but a well-meaning bee!"

**XIII. A Beneficent Bee**: Bee work; John Smith boss. Herbert's rake. Mrs. Smith's dinner; Herbert carries Mrs. Montaigne over wall. Helena refuses to come.

**XIV. An Astonishing Question**: Dorothy feeds Peter a chocolate cake; Peter attaches to her skirt; Helena scorns him; Herbert befriends Peter. Mrs. Cecil sends Dorothy to drive Mr. Smith's old horse. Mrs. Cecil asks Dorothy to become her adopted daughter.

**XV. Concerning Several Matters**: Jim and Dorothy drive; Jim studies; Mrs. Calvert gave Jim books (Shakespeare). Jim's circus plan. Martha's tearful request not to lose Dorothy. Mrs. Calvert's offer declined.

**XVI. The Fate of Daisy-Jewel**: Bee's aftermath; asparagus trench planted (Pa Babcock). Auction of Daisy-Jewel: Seth buys for $35 (Mrs. Calvert's instructions). Dorothy weeps; Jim boards Hannah's horns. Helena sick; Dorothy visits, feeds her. Jim and Dorothy to circus at Newburgh.

**XVII. On the Road to the Circus**: Jim drives runabout; Mrs. Calvert gives Jim day off. Jim plans Headquarters visit. Dorothy confesses she saw the ghost (Peter) in the garden at night. Bill Barry auctions widow's piebald pony; Dorothy bids $35 and buys Portia. Jim buys phaeton and harness for $15. They skip circus.

**XVIII. That South Meadow**: Jim gives phaeton as gift. Dorothy names pony Portia. Mine exploration plan. Oliver Sands offers $200 for south meadow (credited against $300 loan). Martha's bitterness; Pa Babcock's remarks. Dorothy plans picnic at south meadow; saddle from Mrs. Calvert. Surveyors arrive claiming Sands bought the meadow (Martha dismisses them).

**XIX. Dorothy Has Another Secret**: Sands says surveying will proceed. Dorothy gets secret fund from Seth (Kidder & Kidder, Baltimore; hers from a relative). Dorothy discloses Ghost secret to Seth; Seth reveals he's seen ghost. Seth invited to picnic. Dorothy tells cat/secret slip. Picnic at south meadow.

**XX. All's Well That Ends Well**: Shaft found; Peter found living in mine. Herbert descends; snake bites Jim (saves Herbert). Seth cauterizes wound, Peter's herbs. Montaignes invite Dorothy to Europe; she declines. Dorothy pays off Sands ($300 + interest) with secret fund. Syndicate offers iron-mine/mineral spring royalties. Farewell.

## Key Quotes
- "Well, Dorothy, good-by!" (final line)
- "Don't see why." (Jim)
- "Thunder-ation!" (Jim, Seth reveals knowledge)
- "Behold the 'Haunt' of Skyrie!" (Seth)
- "Mis' Calvert's notion..." etc.

## Related Books (catalogue)
Dorothy; Dorothy at Skyrie; Dorothy's Schooling; Dorothy's Travels; Dorothy's House Party; Dorothy in California; Dorothy on a Ranch; Dorothy's House Boat; Dorothy at Oak Knowe; Dorothy's Triumph; Dorothy's Tour.
